comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATIONAL LESSONS (both self-inflicted): (1) editing a ticket's description WHILE its own review-plan run is in flight cancels that run with 'cancelled-stale' and signs nothing - 111a lost a full review this way; settle the plan, THEN review. (2) Running 7 concurrent review-plan processes against one tracker produced a 'store-read-failure' on a4d7 - reduce concurrency to ~4. Also: leaf 1 (6f18) LANDED as gerrit 55e308eaaf via change 2046 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, submitted). Follow-up change 2048 pushed to satisfy 6f18 AC2 (the guard proved it PASSES but never that it FLAGS): extracted paths._offending_line, unit-tested flagging/suppression/reason-less-marker directly, and the tree scan now shares that one classifier instead of re-implementing the match.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: LEAF 1 COMPLETE: 6f18 (unacademic-diabolic-esok) closed after both changes merged (2046 -> 55e308eaaf, 2048 -> 597010b9f1), each LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1. Close passed the completion-verification gate AND the execution-phase plan-review close gate; it unblocked 1cf6. PARALLELISM CORRECTION (user challenge): the earlier 'concurrency ceiling of 3-4' was an unfounded inference from a single store-read-failure under unknown load with 4+ other sessions competing. The real, reproducible blocker is a git ref race - concurrent review-plan runs in ONE checkout each git-fetch and stomp refs/remotes/origin/tickets ('cannot lock ref: is at X but expected Y'); worktrees do not fix it since they share refs/. Mitigation: stagger dispatch 40s so only the brief fetch serialises. Now running 5-8 concurrent reviews cleanly. Investigation+remediation fanned out to read-only subagents that WRITE a full corrected description to tmp/remediation/<id>.md; orchestrator applies rebar edit serially. 14 of 23 plans corrected this way; every single one had material factual errors.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: SIGNING ISSUE HANDED TO /rebar-debug (no assumed root cause). Symptom: 'rebar sign-review <id>' - the documented recovery for a PASS that did not persist - itself fails with {ok:false, signed:false, verdict:PASS, reason:'the attestation could not be persisted: plan review generation remained unstable after 3 attempts'}. Affects 111a-4626-8d2c-42bf, 825c-ba3e-587b-4b7f, 7931-faee-53ba-47b1 (each latest REVIEW_RESULT: verdict PASS, 0 blocking, signature unsigned). Tracebacks: attest.py:202 sign_plan_review -> generation.py:291 sign_manifest -> PlanReviewGenerationError('store-read-failure'); and generation.py:368 -> PlanReviewGenerationRetryable. ~25 rounds of sign-review retry over ~20min recovered none. Prior art, both CLOSED: 790c-a7a3-120a-42c8 (passing review ends unsigned under concurrent writes - its remedy is that sign-review IS the working recovery, which is exactly what fails here) and c083-4d7d-0aca-4e3f (sign-review failing on stray untracked tracker files). CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER CLAIM: I asserted a moving-tickets-HEAD fence as the root cause from reading sign_manifest; that was inference, not evidence, and is NOT to be treated as established.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: SIGNING BUG PROVEN AND FILED: a83f-6348-a08c-401d (georgiaite-flawless-sawfish, p1, open), discovered_from 2ddd, caused_by d70a-d06e-aea0-4008. Root cause proven by hermetic experiment, NOT inference: sign_manifest validates against store-wide tracker HEAD rather than the subject's own generation, at THREE sites - generation.py:292 before/after fence; generation.py:335 under-lock check that is anti-correlated by construction (a process only moves HEAD by committing under that lock, so a blocked acquisition ends just after a HEAD-moving commit); relation_snapshot.py:145 unlocked git status hitting the writer's add->commit gap (58.4% probe failure). Median inter-commit gap on the tracker is 3s and 65 of the last 120 commits are rebar's OWN background enrichment, while collect() takes 3.3-3.7s - so with MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS=3, no backoff and no jitter, the recovery is structurally unable to succeed. CORRECTS MY EARLIER CLAIM that the churn was partly self-inflicted by my ticket edits: it is dominated by rebar's own machinery. The guarding regression test (test_plan_review_generation_scope.py:41, titled 'Signing must survive UNRELATED concurrent tracker writes') monkeypatches tracker_head_sha to a constant so it can never observe the fence firing - the same green-but-vacuous oracle class that sibling ticket d075 exists to catch.

comments.body: 825c (ruinable-cozey-caracal) UNPARENTED from epic 2ddd and force-closed by operator decision: it is not a consolidation. Its three 'copies' of the close-reason/force rule differ in four material ways, decisively CLI-refuses vs library-silently-discards, both pinned - so no merge leaves the suite green and converging either way is a deliberate behaviour change. It would also have violated the epic's own consolidation guarantees (changes pinned behaviour on two surfaces; net additive). Analysis preserved as ticket comments. Residual filed as e1a2-0a03-e26b-416e (unthinking-halfwoolen-anura), linked discovered_from 2ddd: MCP transition_ticket still lacks 'reason' and its strict-xfail row cites scratchy-leprous-galago, which is CLOSED - so the live gap had no open tracker. Also recorded there: adapters.py:442 classifies by signature INTROSPECTION, so a signature-only addition would flip the strict-xfail to xpass while the datum is still discarded.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: STRUCTURAL COST OBSERVED (worth recording for the epic): landing a consolidation change INVALIDATES its own ticket's plan-review attestation, because the review pins the code and the change modifies exactly the files the plan names. 4329's close-review came back 'stale-code: 4 dependency file(s) changed' naming the very files it landed. So each leaf needs a SECOND full plan review after merge purely to satisfy the close gate - roughly doubling LLM spend per leaf. This compounds with bug a83f (the sign fence), because that second review must not only PASS but persist a signature against a tracker that is rarely quiet. Throughput on this epic is now gated by the review/attestation cycle, not by the coding: the three leaves implemented so far each took one implementer pass and first-attempt-green happy paths, while their plans took 2-4 review rounds apiece.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: RETRACTION of the previous entry's generalisation. The observation is sound and directly evidenced: 4329's close-review returned 'stale-code: 4 dependency file(s) changed' naming the files its own change landed - that is the gate reporting its own reason, not my inference. But the conclusions I drew from it - 'roughly doubling LLM spend per leaf' and 'throughput is now gated by the review/attestation cycle' - are UNTESTED extrapolations from a single observation, stated as fact. They do not meet this project's experimental standard and must not be acted on. Standing rule adopted for the rest of this run: any behaviour I classify as a BUG goes through /rebar-debug for a proven, cited root cause before I act on it or record it as established. Applied so far: a83f (sign fence) and de95 (order-dependent flake) were both handed to /rebar-debug rather than diagnosed by me. Not applicable to: correcting my own plan prose to match landed code, which is authoring, not diagnosis.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: FULL RETRACTION (supersedes both prior entries on this topic). My claim that 'landing a change invalidates its own ticket's plan-review attestation' is WITHDRAWN as incorrect. I inferred it from a single gate message ('stale-code: 4 dependency file(s) changed') without reading the currency/drift implementation, and my previous retraction was itself inadequate - it withdrew only the extrapolations while still calling the core claim 'sound and directly evidenced'. It was not: an error message naming changed files is not evidence for a general rule about what invalidates an attestation, and I did not establish what the drift check actually compares. I am deliberately NOT offering a replacement hypothesis. Nothing in this run should be read as an established fact about attestation currency. If this ever needs to be acted on, it goes through /rebar-debug for a proven, cited mechanism. Practically, closing 4329 needs only a current attestation, which requires re-running the review - no theory of the mechanism is required to do that.
